case_title: S. K. Miglani v. State NCT of Delhi
trial_court_outcome: Charged under IPC s. 465 and s. 120-B
neutral_facts: The accused, who was employed as a manager in a nationalized bank, was involved in an incident where a savings account was opened in the name of a person, with forged signatures. The account was used to encash a refund cheque. The investigation revealed that the accused had forged the signature of the allottee on the account opening form. A forensic science laboratory report was obtained to analyze the handwriting on the documents. The accused applied for discharge on the grounds that he was a public servant and that prosecution sanction was required under Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The trial court rejected the application, and the accused challenged the decision in the High Court. The High Court upheld the trial court's decision, and the Supreme Court affirmed this, noting that the accused was not a public servant removable from his office without government sanction, and therefore, Section 197 did not apply. The court deleted the trial court's observation that the accused had committed forgery, as it was premature to make such a conclusion before trial.
